data.name: World Destroyers
data.detailed_description:
World Destroyers is a fast-paced, skill-testing, multiplayer space shooter that pays homage to classic games such as Asteroids, but with modern high-speed action.

Up to four players can team up to save Earth in Story mode, or see how far they can get in the endless Horde and Retro modes. And of course, bring out the trash talk in fully customizable Battle mode.

The Story

When an unusually large cluster of asteroids heads towards Earth, command sends a small fleet of spacecraft to shoot them down. It quickly becomes clear that not all is as it seems. An alien species with sinister intentions threatens to destroy our solar system.


It’s up to you to defend Earth from the dreaded World Destroyers. Huge alien space stations that harvest planets for their resources, leaving destruction in their wake. The aliens have superior weaponry, but perhaps mankind’s remarkable ingenuity can stop their plans.

Features

  • 1 to 4 player mayhem, team up or compete with your friends!
  • Diverse story campaign featuring 40 levels, bonus mini-games, and an EPIC final boss.
  • 5 difficulty modes, from relaxed casual fun to pulse-pounding pull your hair out insane!
  • Arcade modes such as Horde, Battle, Race and Retro.
  • Fully realized mobius levels. Wrap-around edges that both enemies and SKILLED players can take advantage of.
  • An armory of 15 distinct weapons, including 3 super weapons. The Nuke, Deathflower and Vortex Bomb.
  • Master the use of 4 special abilities. The Shield, Repulsor, Auto-Turret, and Warp Drive.
  • Viciously smart enemies, including fighters, UFOs, armored space stations with custom armaments, and of course asteroids!
  • 10 unique destroyer armaments, including hangars, missile launchers, shield generators and laser cannons.
  • Rousing original soundtrack to blow stuff up to!

reviews.review:
World Destroyers is a fast arcade space shooter that takes the basic Asteroids idea and turns it into something much more chaotic. I am flying around open space, shooting asteroids, enemy ships and huge alien stations while trying to survive increasingly difficult waves. The story has me defending Earth from an alien race that travels around destroying planets for their resources, but the story is mostly there to give the shooting a reason to happen. What I actually enjoy is how quickly the game gets me into the action and how much stuff can be happening around me at once.

The campaign is bigger than I expected from such a simple looking game. There are 40 story levels, bonus minigames and five difficulty settings, so I can choose whether I want something fairly relaxed or a much harder challenge. The levels use a wraparound design where going off one side of the screen brings me back from the other side, which adds a little more to the movement than simply staying inside a fixed arena. I have to think about where enemies are coming from and can use the edges of the map to reposition myself when things get crowded.

I also like the amount of weapons and abilities available. There are 15 different weapons, including powerful options such as the Nuke, Deathflower and Vortex Bomb, along with four special abilities covering things like shields, repulsors, an auto turret and a warp drive. That gives me plenty of ways to deal with enemies rather than relying on one basic weapon for the entire game. The larger alien destroyers also have different weapons and systems of their own, so the bigger encounters can feel more involved than simply shooting another asteroid until it disappears.

The extra arcade modes are another good addition. Horde gives me an endless style challenge, while Battle, Race and Retro modes give the basic shooting some different ways to play. The game also supports up to four players locally, with both cooperative and competitive options, which fits the arcade style really well. Even when I am playing alone, I like having those different modes available because they give the game something beyond the main campaign. There are also a huge number of achievements to work through, although I see those more as an extra reason to replay things rather than a major part of the experience.

The biggest weakness for me is that the core gameplay can become repetitive. No matter how many weapons or enemy types are added, I am still flying around and shooting things for most of the experience. That is not necessarily a problem for a game like this, but it does limit how much depth I can expect from it. The visuals are also fairly basic, and while the retro presentation suits the arcade idea, it does not give the game a particularly memorable identity. I also noticed that the game recommends using a controller and admits that the keyboard and mouse controls are not explained very well, which makes the initial experience less friendly than it could be.

I think the game works best when I treat it as a proper old school arcade shooter rather than expecting a modern space adventure. The fast pace, simple objective and large number of weapons make it easy for me to pick up, play for a while and come back to later. I also appreciate that the game is free to play, because the amount of content in the campaign and the extra modes makes that feel like a fair deal. The difficulty options are useful too because I can make the game much more demanding once the easier levels stop giving me enough of a challenge.

Overall, World Destroyers is a fun little space shooter that understands what makes arcade games enjoyable. I like the 40 level campaign, weapon variety, special abilities, wraparound arenas and extra modes, and I think the local four player options give it some nice added value. It does not have enough depth to keep me completely invested for a huge amount of time, and the basic presentation and controls could be better, but the shooting itself is enjoyable and there is more content here than I expected. For me, it is a solid retro inspired action game that is best played in shorter sessions when I want something fast and uncomplicated.

Rating: 6.8/10
